review_scope: Official-site provenance and bounded handoff facts only; not a legal opinion, agency approval, or assurance that an agency will accept or resolve a matter.

sources.title: MHA Cyber and Information Security division: I4C and National Cybercrime Reporting Portal
sources.review_note: Official MHA page identifies I4C and the National Cybercrime Reporting Portal. It does not by itself verify the current public portal TLS certificate.

sources.authority: Department of Consumer Affairs, National Consumer Helpline
sources.title: National Consumer Helpline portal: about, scope, and grievance process
sources.review_note: The portal describes NCH as a pre-litigation consumer grievance mechanism and says an unsatisfied consumer may approach the appropriate Consumer Commission. No remedy is promised.

sources.authority: Department of Consumer Affairs, National Consumer Helpline
sources.title: National Consumer Helpline official contact channels
sources.review_note: Official portal contact channels and stated operating hours reviewed on 2026-10-02.

sources.authority: Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances, Government of India
sources.title: CPGRAMS official portal overview, coverage, exclusions, and appeal information
sources.review_note: Official page limits the portal to public-authority service-delivery grievances and lists RTI, court-related/sub judice, religious, and specified employee-service matters among exclusions.

sources.authority: Department of Personnel and Training, Government of India
sources.title: RTI Online FAQ: Central public authority scope and State exclusion
sources.review_note: FAQ says the portal serves Central Ministries/Departments and Central Public Authorities in its form; State public authority requests, including NCT Delhi, are returned.

sources.authority: National Legal Services Authority, Department of Justice
sources.title: NALSA FAQ: legal services, eligibility, application channels, and helpline
sources.review_note: FAQ describes legal services institutions, Section 12 eligibility categories, application paths, and helpline 15100. The competent institution decides eligibility and action.

sources.authority: Department of Justice, National Legal Services Authority, and CSC e-Governance Services India Limited
sources.title: Tele-Law scheme overview
sources.review_note: Scheme page describes access to legal information/advice through panel lawyers using CSC video or telephone facilities. It does not establish SCMIRN eligibility or advice.

sources.authority: Department of Justice, Government of India, and CSC e-Governance Services India Limited
sources.title: Tele-Law official terms and conditions
sources.review_note: Terms identify the scheme and explicitly caution that website information can change and that law and official instruments prevail.

sources.title: Tele-Law privacy policy and applicant data collection
sources.review_note: Policy describes applicant data collected by Tele-Law. SCMIRN does not collect or forward those application fields; users must review the destination policy before submitting.

services.description: The MHA identifies the National Cybercrime Reporting Portal. The public portal source could not be TLS-verified on 2026-10-02, so this handoff remains unavailable until that source is reviewed again.
services.department: Ministry of Home Affairs, Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre
services.eligibility: Only online financial cyber fraud wording is in scope. The official portal and law-enforcement agency determine complaint handling.
exclusions: This route does not submit a complaint or determine criminal liability.

services.canonical_name: National Consumer Helpline consumer grievance handoff
services.description: Official consumer grievance portal described by the Department of Consumer Affairs as a pre-litigation mechanism. Registration does not guarantee a remedy.
services.eligibility: Consumer issues can be lodged through the official NCH channels. The portal forwards matters to the concerned company, agency, regulator, or ombudsman as applicable.
exclusions: NCH describes this as pre-litigation redress; it is not a court filing or guaranteed remedy.

services.description: Government of India portal for public-authority service-delivery grievances, with tracking and an appeal facility described on the official page.
services.department: Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances
services.eligibility: This handoff is limited to grievances concerning public-authority service delivery, subject to the official portal's own rules.
exclusions: Government employee service matters except where official prior-channel conditions are met

services.canonical_name: RTI Online request for Central public authorities
services.description: DoPT's RTI Online portal serves Central Ministries, Departments, and Central Public Authorities listed in its form. It does not accept State public authority requests, including NCT Delhi.
services.eligibility: The requested authority must be a Central Ministry, Department, or Central Public Authority available in the official RTI Online request form.
exclusions: State and Union Territory public authorities, including NCT Delhi, are outside this portal's stated scope.

services.canonical_name: Legal aid and Tele-Law information handoff
services.description: Official NALSA and Tele-Law channels for information about legal services and access to legal advice. SCMIRN does not assess eligibility or provide legal advice.
services.department: Department of Justice, National Legal Services Authority, and CSC e-Governance Services India Limited
services.eligibility: NALSA/Legal Services Institutions decide legal-aid eligibility and the action on an application. Tele-Law describes access to legal advice through its own official channels.
exclusions: SCMIRN does not decide legal-aid eligibility, provide legal advice, submit an application, or collect application documents.
